external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app and may connect partner apps.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: other companies
external_entities.description: Companies that run partner apps on their own servers.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in, call the rewards API, and retain a refresh token.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server handling member sign-in, authorization code flow, consent, tokens, and partner application authorization.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: A member's sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; nobody decided an idle timeout.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API called by the mobile app that reads and writes the points ledger and handles gift-card redemption.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It does not check which client or which audience a token was issued for.

processes.name: partner app
processes.description: A web application run by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
processes.notes: Every partner app receives every scope. The partner app sends its client secret in the body of its token requests.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account closure state.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction, including the client associated with each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, and not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: Member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: PKCE challenge status is not recorded.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: Mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.notes: Access tokens are plain bearer tokens and live for one hour.

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: Member signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page and approves the consent screen.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: Authorization server returns the browser to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The authorization code remains valid for ten minutes.

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: Partner app sends token requests containing its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The client secret is supplied in the request body.

data_flows.name: take access token
data_flows.description: Support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server
data_flows.notes: The authorization server signs tokens for the support console with the same key used for other tokens.

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: Authorization server stores and retrieves member identity, authorization, token, consent, and account state data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account state

data_flows.name: read and write ledger
data_flows.description: Rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: How the rewards API connects to the ledger was not recorded.

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: Rewards API writes every received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: Support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: Closing an account does not remove that member's refresh tokens.

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud account where the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: member phone
trust_boundaries.description: The member's phone, outside the system's own cloud account.

trust_boundaries.name: partner app server
trust_boundaries.description: A partner company's own server running its partner app.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It stores member email addresses, password hashes, refresh tokens, authorization codes, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It stores every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It stores every request received by the rewards API, including headers, which may contain credentials and personal data.
It is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
